title: Player Settings Deep Dive
description: Configure company name, product name, icons, resolution, splash screen, and other essential settings.

slides.title: Player Settings 🔧
slides.content:
# Global Configuration for Your Build

Click the **Player Settings** button in Build Settings (or Edit → Project Settings → Player). This opens a comprehensive panel with settings specific to the current platform.

It's divided into sections: Company Name, Product Name, Version, Icon, Resolution and Presentation, Splash Image, Other Settings, Publishing Settings.

These settings define how your application appears on the target device.

quizData.question: Where can you change the game's name that appears in the title bar?
quizData.explanation: Product Name under Player Settings sets the application title.

slides.title: Company & Product Names 🏷️
slides.content:
# Identity and Save Paths

- **Company Name** – used for the publisher folder (e.g., `MyCompany`). Affects save file paths on some platforms.
- **Product Name** – the displayed name of your game (title bar, app store).
- **Version** – version string displayed and used for updates.

These are essential for a professional build. They also determine the default data path (`Application.persistentDataPath`).

slides.title: Icon & Cursor 🖼️
slides.content:
# Branding

Under **Icon**, you can assign a default application icon (for desktop and mobile). For Android/iOS, there are adaptive icon settings.

For standalone, you can also set a **Default Cursor** image and hotspot.

All these assets must be imported as textures, and for icons you need specific sizes (e.g., 1024x1024 for iOS).

slides.title: Resolution & Presentation 🖥️
slides.content:
# How the Game Appears

- **Fullscreen Mode** – Exclusive Fullscreen, Fullscreen Window, Windowed.
- **Default Is Fullscreen** – start in fullscreen.
- **Default Width/Height** – resolution when windowed.
- **Resizable Window** – allow user to resize.
- **Run In Background** – continue running when window loses focus.
- **Display Resolution Dialog** – show a settings dialog at startup (standalone only).

For mobile, you control orientation (Portrait, Landscape, Auto) under Resolution and Presentation.

quizData.question: Where do you set the default screen resolution for a Windows build?
quizData.explanation: Resolution settings are in Player Settings.

slides.title: Splash Screen & Other Settings 🌊
slides.content:
# Launch Experience

- **Splash Image** – configure the Unity logo, custom logo, and background shown during loading. (Personal edition always shows 'Made with Unity'.)
- **Other Settings** – rendering API, color space, static/dynamic batching, scripting backend (IL2CPP vs Mono), API compatibility level, target SDK (for Android), etc.
- **Publishing Settings** – keystore for Android, provisioning profiles for iOS, etc.

These settings are critical for performance, compatibility, and store compliance.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Scripting Backend

- **Mono** – fast build, slower runtime. Good for quick testing.
- **IL2CPP** – longer build, better performance and security. Required for iOS and many consoles.
